newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Intel sees 1998 Costa Rica exports of $300 mln.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees 1998 Costa Rica exports of $300 mln.

text.p: U.S. microchip giant Intel Corp expects to export more than $300 million worth of goods from Costa Rica in 1998 during its first year of operations, Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres said on Thursday.
"Intel will produce income equivalent to 80 percent of coffee exports, an activity that's been going on for 150 years in Costa Rica," Figueres said, referring to Costa Rica's traditional top export.
He was speaking at a ceremony to lay the first stone of Intel's plant, expected to cost between $300 million and $500 million.
Intel announced in November its intention to build a plant in Costa Rica with plans to make nearly one-third of all its Pentium II processors here by the end of 1998.
The plant site, about 12 miles northeast of San Jose, used to be a coffee plantation.
The 40,000-square-meter plant is expected to employ about 2,000 people. It is the first Intel plant in Latin America.
